description:
The pet character windows (§7.1) and nothing else: they may receive host events, and they may not read a file, open a dialog, raise a notification or move any window — including their own.

Eight of the app's own commands, one per call the pet's own page and menu make: `desktop_pet_state` (the lifecycle's first read), `desktop_pet_set_visible` (the menu's hide), `desktop_pet_close_own` and `desktop_pet_set_click_through` (its own window, and only its own — both take the caller Tauri reports rather than a label), `desktop_pet_open_settings` (the menu's settings, which names a page and never a window), `desktop_pet_tasks` (the task feed's first read and every re-read after a push), `desktop_pet_appearance` (what the window draws, which resolves one sheet file and no directory), and `desktop_pet_open_task` (the bubble's click, which names a task and never a window).

Deliberately absent, and each for a reason a reader can check: every `agent_*` (a decoration does not start, stop, prompt or authorise a run), every `fs_*` (it reads no vault file), `desktop_pet_open` and `desktop_pet_disable` (creating and tearing down character windows is the settings switch's job, not a decoration's — a pet that could open more pets is a second way to reach the cap), `desktop_pet_windows` and `desktop_pet_capabilities` (the settings page's reports), `desktop_pet_read_settings`/`desktop_pet_update_settings` (writing `general.enabled` is the switch itself), and `desktop_pet_library`/`desktop_pet_import_character` (the character picker and the import dialog, which are the settings page's and which the pet does not need to draw the character it was already told to draw).
